thread.title: A major buying opportunity has been brewing in stocks for weeks

author: Scott Gamm
title: A major buying opportunity has been brewing in stocks for weeks
text:
Traders work on the floor of the NYSE More The thesis of one of Wall Street’s most watched strategists was strengthened by Friday’s better-than-expected jobs report .
On Thursday, Brian Belski, chief investment strategist at BMO Capital Markets, told clients that October’s pullback was “one of the best buying opportunities in several months,” as the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) clocked a 7% loss during the month.
Belski also reminded investors that “positive fundamentals and steady macro data remain in place.”
That was solidified by fresh Friday data showing the addition of 250,000 jobs in October and the 3.1% year-over-year wage growth — the strongest in almost a decade.
Stocks stumbled following the report, as investors fear a more aggressive pace of Federal Reserve rate hikes, though the decline may be more tied to Apple’s ( AAPL ) shocking decision to stop reporting product unit sales figures going forward.
Still, it’s hard to ignore the strong economic fundamentals, even coming off of a bruising month for stocks.
“Friday’s reading suggests that the recent uptrend in hiring activity since late 2017, driven primarily by an acceleration in cyclically-sensitive goods-producing industries, remains intact after a somewhat disappointing September report,” wrote Nomura analysts in a note to clients.
While Bank of America Merrill Lynch analysts warn of noise in the October jobs report amid a spat of recent hurricanes, they acknowledge the broader trend for wages is moving in a positive direction.
“The upward trajectory seen in the wage data over the last few months is a good sign that the tight labor market conditions are finally generating meaningful wage pressures in the economy,” they said in a note to clients Friday.
The spike in wages couldn’t come at a better time, as the all-important holiday shopping season heats up.
“Going into holiday 2018, [the rise in wages] is a good development for stocks from a consumer spending perspective,” said Nick Colas, co-founder of DataTrek Research.
